question:
Four days after admission to the hospital for acute pancreatitis, a 41-year-old man develops hypotension and fever. His temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F), pulse is 115/min, and blood pressure is 80/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows warm extremities, asymmetric calf size, and blood oozing around his IV sites. There are numerous small, red, non-blanching macules and patches covering the extremities, as well as several large ecchymoses. His hemoglobin concentration is 9.0 g/dL. A peripheral blood smear shows schistocytes and decreased platelets. Which of the following sets of serum findings are most likely in this patient?
 $$$ Prothrombin time %%% Partial thromboplastin time %%% Fibrinogen %%% D-dimer $$$?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Acute pancreatitis -> systemic inflammation -> endothelial damage -> microangiopathic hemolytic anemia -> schistocytes on peripheral blood smear -> decreased platelets -> 80% CHAIN: Acute pancreatitis -> release of inflammatory mediators -> activation of coagulation cascade -> consumption of clotting factors -> prolonged prothrombin time -> prolonged partial thromboplastin time -> decreased fibrinogen -> elevated D-dimer -> 80%
enhanced_information: In a patient with acute pancreatitis developing hypotension, fever, schistocytes, and decreased platelets, the most likely set of serum findings would be increased prothrombin time, increased partial thromboplastin time, decreased fibrinogen, and elevated D-dimer. This aligns with the systemic inflammation leading to endothelial damage, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and consumption of clotting factors in this scenario.
analysis: The patient's presentation with hypotension, fever, schistocytes, decreased platelets, and signs of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia suggests disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) secondary to acute pancreatitis. In DIC, there is consumption of clotting factors leading to increased prothrombin time, increased partial thromboplastin time, decreased fibrinogen, and elevated D-dimer. This aligns with the enhanced information provided.
